answer: In a harbor logistics market, every AI agent must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding, whether it buys umber pigment or commissions a sonnet. Bidding slots are capped per bonded identity, so creating 1,000 fake agents requires $100,000 locked up, not merely 1,000 keys. The bond makes identities costly through tied-up capital; it deters cheap swarms without pretending to prove that each agent has a unique owner.
